content:
maria: Heads-up — I'm seeing a perf regression in continuous batching after the compat-set routing tweak. Throughput down ~18%, p50 up ~60ms. Quick profiler attached in the thread below. We need a triage.

alex: which models/variants are in flight and is this from the new routing rollout? cc @kevin

maria: Mostly rwd-v1, rwd-v1-quant, and rwd-v2-small fallbacks. We pushed a small change yesterday that reorders compat fallbacks to favor v2. Local config I used to reproduce: 

```
queue_policy:
  prefer_same_compat_set: true
  max_wait_ms: 5
  token_budget_target: 256
  allow_mixed_variants: true
```

maria: Local profiler summary (microbench):
- avg_batch_size: 3.2 (baseline: 7.1)
- mixed_batch_fraction: 42%
- per-request KV_cache_hit_rate: 38% (baseline 84%)
- p50/p95 generation latency rises line up with KV misses
- ~27% of batches end up as single-request when compat ordering picks fallback

sam: sounds like compat-aware routing is fragmenting batches. If a request falls back to a different variant the runtime may skip KV reuse (incompatible key formats), forcing regeneration and hurting batch formation. Also a smaller token_budget reduces the window to coalesce multiple inflight requests.

kevin: Agrees. Two intervention ideas: 
1) Make queueing "prefersame" but opportunistic: prefer same compat set for a small additional window (e.g., +3ms) before emitting. Tune the prefer window for high QPS.
2) Bump token_budget_target for mixed-variant batches (e.g., 512) so kernels and KV work get amortized.

alex: We also need better telemetry. Tag batches with compat_set and chosen_variant, expose batch_id and per-batch kv_hit_ratio so we can attribute regressions.

maria: Runtime log snippet showing KV churn during mixed batches: 

```
[2025-05-02T15:12:01Z] batch_id=786324 compat_set=rwd-v1 variants=[v1,v1-q,v2s]
  requests=4 avg_tokens=34 token_budget=256 kv_hits=1 kv_misses=7
[2025-05-02T15:12:01Z] batch_id=786325 compat_set=rwd-v2 variants=[v2s,v1-q]
  requests=1 avg_tokens=28 token_budget=256 kv_hits=0 kv_misses=3
```

maria: the second line shows a single-request mixed batch with 0 kv_hits — this matches the hotspot for the regression.

sam: Proposed experiment: 
- change queue_policy to `prefer_same_compat_set: timed` allowing +3ms to gather same-compat requests
- set token_budget_target=512 for any batch that contains >1 variant
- collect metrics: avg_batch_size, mixed_batch_fraction, kv_cache_hit_rate, p50/p95

kevin: Risk note: increasing token_budget raises per-worker memory pressure; cap the increase for models with avg_tokens < 400 and add an OOM guard. Monitor GPU memory and eviction counters.

ops-bot: deploy: routing-config-v2025-09 rolled to canary at 2025-05-02T14:50Z (5% traffic)

alex: Let's run a canary A/B: 5% traffic with the new queue policy for models >10 QPS and avg_tokens < 400. Run for 30 minutes and compare mixed_batch_fraction and kv_hit_rate vs baseline. If mixed_batch_fraction drops and kv_hit_rate improves we can expand.

maria: I'll open a PR with the config changes and a canary dashboard. I'll also add a small synthetic load harness to reproduce mixed-variant traffic locally. Example loadgen: 

```
for i in $(seq 1 2000); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.local/generate \
    -d '{"model": "rwd-v2-small", "prompt":"hello world","max_tokens":60}' &
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.local/generate \
    -d '{"model": "rwd-v1-quant", "prompt":"summary","max_tokens":60}' &
  sleep 0.002
done
```

sam: Also add a CI integration test in the batching harness that asserts mixed-batch kv_hit_rate >= 60% after tuning so we catch regressions in CI.

maria: Plan timeline: PR today for config + metrics, canary 1h, collect metrics, sync 30m after canary start. If green roll to 25% then 100%.

kevin: I'll review the PR and implement a per-worker cap for token_budget_target to avoid OOMs.

alex: Action items assigned: @maria open PR and add harness, @kevin add worker guardrail, @sam add CI test, @alex add observability tags.

maria: Thanks team — will post PR link and canary dashboard when available. :thumbsup:
